title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-jon-wip
content:
Summary:
- Spike/drop in distributed traces and per-request metrics starting ~2026-02-24 03:10 UTC. Logs ingestion also shows gaps for services frontend-api and model-router in the same time window.

Symptoms observed:
- Grafana: p50/p95 latency metrics unchanged but request-count and error-rate metrics drop ~40% for frontend-api between 03:08-03:22 UTC.
- Jaeger/Tempo: traces for frontend-api -> model-router hops missing; traces that do appear end at model-router ingress.
- Loki: log streams from frontend-api show a 15-minute gap aligning with metrics drop.
- Kafka metrics: consumer group for obs-ingest (group obs-ingest-frontend) shows growing lag from 03:05 onwards.
- Fluentd/Vector logs on obs-ingest-01: frequent WARN about "failed to parse OTLP envelope" starting 03:06.

Commands run / outputs (copied snippets):
1) kubectl -n observability logs obs-ingest-01 -c vector --since=30m
2026-02-24T03:06:11Z WARN vector::topology::builder: failed to parse OTLP envelope: invalid proto: unknown field 17
2026-02-24T03:06:12Z INFO vector::sink::kafka: send to topic=obs-raw successful batch=1200
2026-02-24T03:07:02Z WARN vector::topology::builder: failed to parse OTLP envelope: invalid proto: unknown field 17

2) kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest-frontend
CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
partition 0  421000  445600  24500
partition 1  419810  445400  25600
(note: lag grows steadily from ~03:05)

3) curl -sS -X GET http://frontend-api.prod/_health | jq .
{"status":"ok","otlp_forwarder":"ok","tracing_enabled":true}
(frontend reports healthy and tracing_enabled=true)

4) tcpdump on obs-ingest-01: observed OTLP gRPC traffic from frontend-exporter (10.3.5.12) to obs-ingest-01:4317, payload size ~2.5kB. Packets show gRPC frames but Vector logs say invalid proto.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Exporter changes (frontend or SDK) started sending OTLP in a different proto version/format (e.g., moved from OTLP v0.9 to v1beta) and Vector/collector config doesn't accept new envelope -> parse failures -> messages dropped -> Kafka consumer sees fewer messages -> metrics/traces/logs vanish.
- H2: A partial config rollout updated Vector/collector parsing rules (a filter/transform) that rejects envelopes with unknown attribute 17. Recent config PR merged ?/78 looks suspicious.
- H3: Network/Ingress change (Envoy sidecar or MTLS enforcement) truncating gRPC frames; but tcpdump shows intact frames so less likely.
- H4: Kafka broker intermittent GC/restart causing increasing lag; however broker metrics don't show restarts and other consumer groups unaffected.

Investigation notes / breadcrumbs:
- PR review: github PR 78 (obs-pipeline-config) changed the OTLP parsing plugin version and tightened schema validation. It was rolled out 2026-02-24 02:50 UTC to obs-ingest nodes via k8s rolling update.
- Rollout timeline matches symptom onset (~03:06), which is ~35-40m after rollout began (rolling update staggered across pods).
- Canary pod (obs-ingest-00) upgraded first and shows no parse errors in log; later pods (obs-ingest-01..03) show warnings. Need to check which plugin version each pod runs.

Config checks performed:
- kubectl -n observability get daemonset obs-ingest -o yaml | grep image
  obs-ingest-image: vector:0.XX -> confirms vector image bumped in new DaemonSet revision.
- kubectl -n observability exec obs-ingest-01 -- cat /etc/vector/vector.toml | grep "otlp" -n
  (found strict attribute whitelist block in newer config)

Quick reproducible test:
- On a dev box, used docker image vector:0.XX + sample OTLP payload produced by otelcol v0.47 -> vector logs same parse error.
- Using otelcol v0.46 payload -> accepted. Suggests proto/field-level incompatibility between client payload and vector plugin.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Rolled back DaemonSet to previous revision on obs-ingest nodes (kubectl rollout undo ds/obs-ingest) in staging first. Observed traces start flowing on staging within ~2 mins.
- Temporarily increased consumer group parallelism and retention as buffer (kafka topic config) while investigating.
- Opened hotfix PR to adjust vector config to be permissive for unknown fields (linked PR).

Errors / logs to reference:
- vector WARN: "failed to parse OTLP envelope: invalid proto: unknown field 17" (repeated ~every 5-10s per upstream host)
- frontend exporter debug: "exporter: grpc send OK, resp: 200" (seems to believe it forwarded successfully)

Open questions:
- Which component introduced field 17? (Could be OpenTelemetry SDK bump in frontend libs or model-router).
- Do other language SDKs produce the field? Our metrics show only frontend-api and model-router impacted -> likely those services recently updated.
- Is it safe to loosen validation in Vector? Risk: accept malformed/malicious payloads; but keeping strictness blocks production telemetry.

Next steps (ordered):
1) Identify exact commit that added unknown field 17: grep recent deps/CHANGELOGs for OTLP changes in frontend-api and model-router.
2) Confirm vector plugin version and the proto definitions shipped in vector:0.XX. Open issue with Vector repo if mismatch.
3) Revert cluster rollout fully to previous vector image (we started partial rollback; confirm all pods are on previous revision) if current hotfix PR not merged.
4) Add compatibility test to CI: send synthetic OTLP payloads from multiple otelcol versions to our vector image to detect proto regressions.
5) Update observability runbook: include steps for detecting "failed to parse OTLP envelope" and immediate rollback commands.
6) Postmortem draft (link placeholder) and schedule follow-up to decide permanent fix (upgrade otlp parsing lib vs. pin exporters).

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- We should consider adding a canary that sends varied OTLP payloads after infra changes to avoid silent breaks.
- Improve logging: include exporter sdk version/hostname in vector warn logs (if available) so we can map which client is sending new fields.

Related artifacts / refs:
- JIRA INF-3214: "OTLP parse failures causing metrics/traces drop" (assigned to me)
- GH PR 78: config change that introduced stricter validation -> suspect
- GH hotfix PR 81: temporary permissive validation change (WIP)
- Confluence draft: OBS-2026-pipeline-postmortem (link above)

If anyone reading: ping @Maya/@Priya if you have context on recent frontend-api SDK bumps. I'll keep updating this doc as I triage.

-- Jon
